L1: # Efficacy of closed reduction surgery on treatment of nasal bone fracture in admitted patients to Shahid Bahonar Hospital, Kerman, Iran

L18: Abstract
L19: BACKGROUND AND AIM: Nasal fracture is one of the most common facial fractures and the main goal of this study was evaluation of closed reduction surgery of nasal bone fractures.METHODS: Thirty six patients including 24 male and 12 female patients suffered from nasal bone fractures were treated by closed reduction method. Preoperative and postoperative computed tomographic scans were analyzed by an expert panel.
L20: Statistical methods including chi-square, Fisher's exact test and regression were used to evaluate the relationship between age, sex and type of trauma and to evaluate the efficacy of closed reduction technique.RESULTS: Type of trauma, age and sex had not any effect on closed reduction efficacy.
L21: We had 36.1% complete success rate (nearly complete anatomic reduction), 36.1% favorable success rate (acceptable non-anatomic reduction) and 27.8% absolute failure (no acceptable reduction) after treatment of nasal bone fractures by closed reduction method.CONCLUSION: Closed nasal reduction is the most commonly used technique for a fractured nose, but it has high degree of failure of treatment, so when choosing the closed reduction method for treatment of nasal bone fractures, appropriate radiography must be taken for meticulous evaluation to reducing the complications.

L36@P0: likely target for traumatic injuries.1-4 Blunt
L37@P0: traumas such as car accidents, sport injuries
L38@P0: and fights are the most prevalent causes of
L39@P0: nasal fracture.3,5,6
L40@P0: Nasal fractures often include multiple
L41@P0: traumas and several models, based on fracture
L42@P0: site and force intensity and direction, have
L43@P0: been proposed for classification purposes.1,6,7
L44@P0: Nasal bone reduction methods include open
L45@P0: reduction and close reduction.4 Close
L46@P0: reduction treatment is mostly used in the early
L47@P0: stages of trauma due to its simplicity and
L48@P0: minimal side effects. However, there is a 14%
L49@P0: to 50% chance of deformity which may require
L50@P0: future septoplasty and rhinoplasty.5,8,9
L51@P0: In addition, some studies have introduced
L52@P0: drawbacks of closed reduction. DeFatta et al.
L53@P0: concluded that in the closed reduction group of
L54@P0: their study, 60% of patients had significant
L55@P0: postoperative septal deviation whereas only
L56@P0: 12.5% suffered from residual septal deformity in
L57@P0: the open reduction group.10 Besides, in the study
L58@P0: of Adami Dehkordi et al., they showed that the

L69@P1: that treatment of acutely fractured nose with

L71@P1: reduction, septoplasty, osteotomies, release of

L74@P1: of the ethmoid, and camouflaging cartilage

L77@P1: It is necessary to explain that usefulness of
L78@P1: conventional (plain) radiographies for clinical
L79@P1: decision making is highly controversial and
L80@P1: computed tomography (CT) has been shown
L81@P1: to be a more accurate diagnostic tool
L82@P1: compared to conventional radiography for
L83@P1: evaluating nasal bone fractures.12-15
L84@P1: So due to greater sensitivity and specificity
L85@P1: of CT scan in comparison with conventional
L86@P1: radiography and the presence of the above
L87@P1: mentioned controversies, we decided to
L88@P1: perform this research and investigate the
L89@P1: position of the fractured segments with
L90@P1: attention to more details by taking pre- and
L91@P1: post-operative CT scans and then comparing
L92@P1: them together to measure the efficacy of
L93@P1: closed reduction for treatment of nasal bone
L94@P1: fractures. For meticulous evaluation of closed
L95@P1: reduction method, we considered the nearly
L96@P1: complete anatomic reduction as complete
L97@P1: success of treatment, acceptable non-anatomic
L98@P1: reduction as favorable success and no
L99@P1: acceptable reduction as absolute failure.
L100@P1: Methods
L101@P1: Patients admitted to Oral and Maxillofacial
L102@P1: Ward of Shahid Bahonar Hospital, Kerman,
L103@P1: Iran, from 23/8/2014 to 21/3/2015 were
L104@P1: enrolled in this study. The inclusion criteria
L105@P1: consisted of all patients with isolated nasal bone
L106@P1: fractures and the exclusion criteria consisted of
L107@P1: patients who had old nasal fractures, open nasal
L108@P1: fractures and comminuted nasal fractures. Based
L109@P1: on the inclusion and exclusion criteria, 36
L110@P1: qualified patients were chosen.
L111@P1: First, CT scan of the patients with coronal
L112@P1: and axial cuts was obtained (Toshiba Co.,
L113@P1: Aquilion model, Japan); then, under general
L114@P1: anesthesia, closed reduction surgery was done
L115@P1: by oral and maxillofacial surgery residents.
L116@P1: After stabilization of the patient’s general
L117@P1: condition in the first day of the surgery, a CT
L118@P1: scan with the same machine, same radiology
L119@P1: technician and similar conditions of radiation
L120@P1: exposure was obtained. CT scans were taken
L121@P1: after careful explanation to the patients and an
L122@P1: informed written consent form was obtained
L123@P1: from each patient.
L124@P1: The study was approved by Vice Deputy of
L125@P1: Research at Kerman University of Medical
L126@P1: Sciences. For the purpose of this research, all
L127@P1: personal information was excluded from both
L128@P1: pre-operation and post-operation CT scans and
L129@P1: coded stereotypes were presented to expert
L130@P1: panel. The expert panel comprised of two oral
L131@P1: and maxillofacial surgeons and two radiology
L132@P1: specialists who had no information about the
L133@P1: patients. Coded stereotypes were analyzed and
L134@P1: interpreted by the expert panel and the quality
L135@P1: of reduction was reported in terms of complete
L136@P1: success rate (nearly complete anatomic
L137@P1: reduction), favorable success rate (acceptable
L138@P1: non-anatomic reduction) and absolute failure
L139@P1: (no acceptable reduction). In cases of complete
L140@P1: success, all broken bones were relocated in
L141@P1: their anatomic position (Figure 1).

L161@P2: Results
L162@P2: This study investigated the data of 36
L163@P2: patients who were admitted in the oral and
L164@P2: Maxillofacial Surgery Ward of Shahid
L165@P2: Bahonar Hospital. The patient’s age range
L166@P2: was between 13-56 years with the average of
L167@P2: 29.86 ± 10.5 years. The highest percentage of
L168@P2: patients (55.6%) belonged to the age group of
L169@P2: 20-30 and the age groups of 10-20 and 50-60
L170@P2: had the lowest number of nasal fracture.
L171@P2: Among the 36 patients of the study, 12 were
L172@P2: female (33.3%) and 24 were male (66.7%),
L173@P2: which shows that the number of male
L174@P2: patients were twice as the number of female
L175@P2: patients. Causes of nasal trauma in this study
L176@P2: consisted of three categories as fights,
L177@P2: accidents and falls. Among these, there were
L178@P2: 7 cases of fight (19.4%), 26 cases of car
L179@P2: accident (72.2%) and 3 cases of fall (8.3%).
L180@P2: Based on the type of nasal fracture, 12
L181@P2: patients (33.3%) had unilateral simple
L182@P2: fractures, 22 patients (61.1%) showed signs of
L183@P2: bilateral simple fractures and 2 patients
L184@P2: (5.6%) had bilateral fractures with septum
L185@P2: fracture. Among these, the unilateral simple
L186@P2: fracture and bilateral fracture with septum
L187@P2: fracture, with respectively 61.1% and 5.6%,
L188@P2: showed the lowest and highest frequency.
L189@P2: Based on treatment effectiveness, 13 cases
L190@P2: had complete reduction (36.1%), 13 cases had
L191@P2: favorable reduction (36.1%) and 10 cases had
L192@P2: absolute failure (27.8%) (Table 1).
L193@P2: Chi-square test was used to study the
L194@P2: relationship between treatment effectiveness
L195@P2: and age, gender, cause of trauma and type of
L196@P2: nasal fracture; however, no significant
L197@P2: relationship was identified. This showed that
L198@P2: age, gender, cause of trauma and kind of
L199@P2: nasal fracture had no impact on the chosen
L200@P2: treatment. In terms of treatment effectiveness,
L201@P2: there was no significant and meaningful
L202@P2: difference between complete success,
L203@P2: favorable success and absolute failure
L204@P2: treatments. However, classification of
L205@P2: treatments into two categories of acceptable
L206@P2: reduction (including full and optimal
L207@P2: reductions) and unacceptable reduction
L208@P2: (including insufficient reduction) showed a
L209@P2: significant and meaningful treatment
L210@P2-3: effectiveness (P = 0.008). http://johoe.kmu.ac.ir, 5 June

L251@P3: Discussion
L252@P3: According to the results of this study, if
L253@P3: absolute success in reduction of nasal bone
L254@P3: fracture was considered as the optimum
L255@P3: treatment, then the closed reduction
L256@P3: procedures would not be a sufficient and
L257@P3: suitable treatment for most cases of nasal
L258@P3: bone fractures. Our finding is compatible
L259@P3: with research done by DeFatta et al. that
L260@P3: stated in the closed reduction group of their
L261@P3: patients, 60% had significant postoperative
L262@P3: septal deviation.10 In addition, Staffel stated
L263@P3: that acute fractures yielded straighter noses
L264@P3: with an individually tailored protocol of
L265@P3: closed reduction, septoplasty, osteotomies,
L266@P3: release of the upper lateral cartilages, fracture
L267@P3: of the anterior extension of the perpendicular
L268@P3: plate of the ethmoid, and camouflaging
L269@P3: cartilage grafts compared to treatment by
L270@P3: closed reduction alone.5 Adami Dehkordi and
L271@P3: et al. have shown that the most
L272@P3: dissatisfaction of their patients belonged to
L273@P3: closed reduction group of nasal bone
L274@P3: fractures with symptoms like nasal hump,
L275@P3: obstruction of nose, deviated nose, and
L276@P3: dysmorphology of nasal septum.11

L283@P4: In the present study, the highest rate of
L284@P4: nasal fracture was observed among the age
L285@P4: group of 20-30 years (55.6%) and the lowest
L286@P4: prevalence was observed in age groups of 10-
L287@P4: 20 years (8.3%) and 50-60 years (8.3%) that is
L288@P4: compatible with the study of Cavalcanti and
L289@P4: Melo that demonstrated 13-17-year-old
L290@P4: teenagers had the highest rate of fractures17
L291@P4: and with Hwang et al. study that showed the
L292@P4: highest incidence of nasal fractures was
L293@P4: among the age group of 11-20 years.12
L294@P4: In this study, 61.1% of the patients had
L295@P4: simple (without comminution) bilateral
L296@P4: fractures, while 33.3% had simple one-sided
L297@P4: fractures and 5.6% showed signs of bilateral
L298@P4: fractures with nasal septum fracture. Since
L299@P4: most septum fractures require open reduction
L300@P4: or septoplasty treatment, were excluded these
L301@P4: patients from our study which yielded to low
L302@P4: prevalence of septum fracture.
L303@P4: There was no significant relationship
L304@P4: between the effectiveness of close reduction
L305@P4: treatment and age, gender, cause of trauma
L306@P4: and type of nasal fracture.
L307@P4: In overall view, closed reduction of nasal
L308@P4: bone fractures is an easy procedure performed
L309@P4: routinely for treatment of this type of nasal
L310@P4: fractures, but the failure of this method is
L311@P4: relatively high, and therefore we recommend
L312@P4: that every patient suffering from nasal bone
L313@P4: fractures must be evaluated individually by
L314@P4: thorough clinical and radiographic
L315@P4: examination and by taking appropriate CT
L316@P4: scan if needed before attempting closed
L317@P4: reduction techniques. If the operator has
L318@P4: doubt for efficacy of closed reduction method,
L319@P4: then it is advised to do open reduction surgery
L320@P4: instead to minimize future complications.
L321@P4: Conclusion
L322@P4: We must cautiously use closed reduction
L323@P4: method for treatment of nasal bone fractures in
L324@P4: selected patients, not routinely. Clinical and
L325@P4: radiographic examination especially CT scan
L326@P4: should be performed when deciding between
L327@P4: closed versus open reduction for treatment of
L328@P4: nasal bone fractures.
